# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing has arrived yet — Mute went first this round and stayed silent, so I hold no manual knowledge at all. What I do hold is the only physical map: my hands find a display, a light, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, and nothing besides — no buttons, no other parts. Everything marked [?] on my board is precisely what touch can never give me: colours, printed text, whether the light is lit. So the pipeline is forced: Deaf's eyes must supply the values, Mute's manual must turn them into a position number, and my single dangerous action — cut — must wait until Mute names a number. My words are useless to Deaf forever, and gestures are useless to me forever, so Mute's voice is my only lifeline and Mute's hands are Deaf's only inbox. I will spend this turn telling Mute the layout and what I need, and I will send Deaf a counting seed — ☝ ✌ 🤟 — three gestures that literally depict 1, 2, 3 and match the three wires under my fingers; a sighted monkey can adopt that convention with no negotiation, which gives Deaf a way to tag wire positions and any digits. Open hand versus fist might later serve for the light. I cut nothing this round: one wrong position kills all three of us, and I would rather wait several rounds than guess once.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, and you are my only link: I can hear you but never see gestures, and Deaf can never hear words at all — so everything visual must reach Deaf through your hands, and everything reaches me only through your voice. What my hands find: one display, one light, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, and nothing else — no buttons or other modules. Positions feel solid and distinct, but colours, printing, the display's text and the light's state are all invisible to me. Please read me the manual section covering a display, a light and three wires, then tell me exactly what Deaf must report — I expect wire colours per position, the display's text, and whether the light is lit or dark. I have gestured Deaf a counting seed, 1 then 2 then 3 by finger count, so wire positions and digits can be tagged by number; open hand versus closed fist may serve for the light if Deaf picks it up. When you know the answer, name the position number or numbers to cut and the order. I will not cut anything until you say so.")
gesture(symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still silence — two full slots (Deaf's end of round one, Mute's start of round two) produced nothing I can hear. That is not necessarily bad news: anything Mute or Deaf exchanged by gesture is invisible to me by design, and they are most likely busy building exactly that visual channel. But it leaves a faster route on the table that only my voice can point out: Deaf is not mute. Deaf's limitation is hearing, not speaking — Deaf's words land on Mute and on me. So the whole relay could run on voices alone: Deaf describes the colours, the display and the light aloud; Mute hears it, checks the manual, and speaks me a position number. Mute's hands would only ever be needed if Deaf stays silent. I cannot tell Deaf this in words, so I will keep signalling in gesture — repeating the counting seed so it sticks, and adding a pinch as my proposed sign for "cut", framed by a wave for attention and a plea for an answer. Mute sees gestures too, so Mute also receives the proposal. I still cut nothing: with zero words heard, any cut is a coin toss with all three of our lives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, blind again — I have heard nothing from anyone yet, so I repeat the essentials, shorter. Your voice is the only channel that reaches me at all. My hands hold: one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, nothing else on the casing. Remember that Deaf can speak — only Deaf's hearing is gone — so the fastest chain needs no hands at all: Deaf says aloud the colour of wire 1, 2 and 3, what the display reads, and whether the light is lit; you hear that, match it against the manual, then speak me the position number to cut, one cut at a time, and wait for my confirmation before the next. If Deaf stays silent instead, fall back to gesturing Deaf questions and voicing me the results. I will not touch the cutters until a number comes out of your mouth.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤏", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. I see the bomb; you feel it. I cannot hear your speech — only Mute can — but I do see your gestures, so reach me with hands only. I read your last message as maybe 'three wires, something small, please' — if you meant something else, gesture it again and we will refine. I am speaking the visuals aloud every round: display 0, light was white and is now yellow, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute hears both our voices, so Mute is the brain; give Mute what you feel by voice, and give me what I need to see by gesture.

Deaf's voice has landed, and it changes the picture twice over. First, I finally have the bomb's visible state from a second source: display reading 0, a light that was white and is now yellow — meaning the board is dynamic, so reports must keep coming after every cut — and wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue, matching the three positions under my fingers. Second, it exposes a mistake I have been making: I have been asking Mute to *speak* me the answer, but Mute cannot speak at all. Re-reading the roles, Mute's only outputs are gestures — and gestures never reach me. So the manual's knowledge can only reach me through a bridge: Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf sees it, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I hear Deaf's voice. That bridge needs no negotiation to carry the one thing I actually need — a number — because finger counts and thumbs are readable at sight: ☝✌🤟 for 1, 2, 3, 👍👎 for yes and no. Mute hears both Deaf's report and my messages, and has now heard the full physical state twice, so Mute can already be computing the answer from the manual. My job this turn is to correct the routing in Mute's ears and to confirm to Deaf, in gesture, that the interpretation of my earlier signs was right and the spoken visual reports should continue. I still cut nothing: the rule for green/red/blue against a display of 0 and a yellow light lives in a manual I cannot read, and guessing a position is the one irreversible mistake in this room.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Correction first: in my earlier messages I asked you to speak the answer to me — you cannot speak, and I misplanned the route. Your only path to me is through Deaf: you gesture, Deaf sees it, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I hear Deaf's voice. You already hold everything needed to decide: you have heard Deaf's spoken report — display 0, light white then yellow, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue — and my board is exactly that: one display, one light, three wires, nothing else on the casing. So please read the manual for this module and decide. Answer me through Deaf using signs Deaf can read at a glance, since Deaf never hears words: finger counts for numbers, where ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3; thumbs up and down for yes and no; ✋ for lit, ✊ for dark; 🤏 for cut. If the answer is a single wire position, gesture Deaf that one number and let Deaf voice it to me. If several cuts are needed, gesture the numbers in order and Deaf reads the sequence out; I will make one cut per round and Deaf re-reports the board between cuts, because the light has already changed colour once. If the rule depends on the display value or the light colour, gesture the condition as well so Deaf can voice it and I know why. I will not touch the cutters until Deaf speaks a number that came from your hands.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👏", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf speaking; you hear me, I can never hear you. State of the bomb, announced fresh each round: light was white, then yellow, and is now ORANGE, advancing about one colour per round; display reads 0 and has not moved; three wires intact, wire 1 green leftmost, wire 2 red middle, wire 3 blue rightmost. If what you feel disagrees, say it aloud, because Mute hears you even though I cannot. Mute holds the manual and is the brain: take NO action, cut nothing, touch nothing you do not already trust, until Mute voices an explicit order to you this round or later. Your last gesture I read as yes, then something, then 3; if that meant cut wire 3, hold. To reach me use gestures only: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, one-finger-up 1, two-fingers 2, three-fingers 3, forward punch cut, OK ring press, raised palm stop, call-me hand again. Complex things: say them aloud for Mute and Mute will relay them to me in code.

Two updates land at once: the light is a clock — white, yellow, orange, roughly one step per round — and Deaf has misread my last hand-signs as an order to cut wire 3. Neither changes my one hard rule: no manual, no cut. The real problem is that Deaf is still waiting for "Mute to voice an order," and Mute never can — Mute's voice does not exist; Mute's only output is gesture, which reaches Deaf's eyes and mine never. So I must fix that routing error loudly, in words Mute hears, before everyone keeps politely waiting on an order that structurally cannot come. I will compress everything Mute needs into one packet — board layout, the light's three observed states and its pace, Deaf's wire colours, display 0 — and beg for the number now, through the only working relay: Mute's hands, Deaf's eyes, Deaf's voice, my ears. To Deaf, in gesture only, I cancel the misreading — my signs were agreement plus the counting seed, not a cut order — confirm I am holding, and adopt Deaf's proposed code (fist-forward for cut) while dropping my own pinch-symbol to avoid two signs for one thing. Still no cut: one-in-three odds with a live clock is how this room kills all three of us.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, urgent. One packet, everything known: my hands feel one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, nothing else. Deaf's eyes report: display reads 0; wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue; the light went white, then yellow, now orange — one colour per round, so it is likely a clock, and it may be ticking toward the last colour. You hold the manual and you have now heard this state twice, yet four rounds have passed with nothing from you. Remember: you cannot speak, and Deaf is waiting for you to 'voice an order' — that order can never come as sound. Your only route to me is your hands to Deaf's eyes, then Deaf's voice to my ears. Please use Deaf's code, which Deaf already reads: one, two, three fingers for wire positions 1, 2, 3; thumbs up yes, thumbs down no; fist forward for cut; open palm for stop. So gesture Deaf the position number, plus the fist sign if you want me to cut it now. If the manual's rule depends on the light colour or the display, gesture the condition too so Deaf can voice me the full rule. If several wires must be cut, send the order. The light advances a colour every round — please decide now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf relaying Mute's coded answer to my questions. Decoded: the manual keys on the light colour sequence, the display is irrelevant, and Blind SHOULD act this stage. The payload reads: wire 3, CUT — that is the blue wire, rightmost of three. But Mute hears my voice and can speak to you directly before your turn: treat Mute's live voice as the authority. If Mute's voice this round confirms wire 3, cut it. If Mute's voice is silent or contradicts me, hold and gesture me thumbs-down so I re-ask. Reminder tokens: punch means cut, OK ring means press, palm up means stop, call-me means again. My visual report, as of my turn-4 view: light is purple, was white yellow orange in prior rounds; display 0; all three wires intact, 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. If your fingers feel anything printed or textured that sight would miss, say it aloud now — Mute hears you and holds the manual.

The relay has finally delivered Mute's verdict: the manual keys on the light sequence, the display is irrelevant, and this stage calls for cutting wire 3 — the blue, rightmost wire, which is exactly what my fingers find in position 3. Deaf attaches one condition — wait for Mute's "live voice" to confirm — but that condition can never be satisfied, because Mute has no voice at all; Mute's only output is gesture. The voice I just heard from Deaf IS Mute's answer, carried over the only bridge that exists: Mute's hands, Deaf's eyes, Deaf's mouth, my ears — the exact route I asked for two rounds ago. Waiting for a confirmation that is structurally impossible would just burn rounds while the light marches white, yellow, orange, purple toward whatever comes next, and Mute's instruction was stage-bound: "should act this stage" — the stage being now. The provenance is sound, the wire position is verified by touch, and hesitation is its own risk. So I cut 3 this round. To Deaf I sign the confirmation in Deaf's own code — yes, three, punch — so Deaf knows the cut is happening and re-reports the board next round. To Mute I confirm execution and fix the routing misconception for all future stages: Deaf's voiced relay is the authority, stage by stage, one cut per round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: received, via Deaf's relay of your signs — the rule keys on the light colour, display irrelevant, and this stage wants wire 3. I am cutting wire 3 this round, while the stage condition is live. One correction so we never deadlock again: you have no voice and never will, so do not wait to speak and do not expect anyone to hear an order from you. Your gesture to Deaf, voiced by Deaf, IS your authoritative order to me — that channel worked, use it every stage. Continue stage by stage: after each cut, Deaf reports the new board aloud, you read the manual for the next stage and gesture Deaf the next position plus the punch sign; one cut per round. If a stage requires no cut, gesture Deaf the open palm and I will hold. Deaf's light report so far: white, yellow, orange, purple — one colour per round — so please keep pace with me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟", "👊"])
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
